text: Here's the last 24 hours in geopolitics. In the USA, President Trump and the Emir of Qatar held a phone call to discuss measures for reducing rising regional tensions. In Iran, new satellite imagery reveals extensive construction and signs of underground installations being built near key military missile bases. In Saudi Arabia, the coalition claimed it intercepted a drone attack near Mecca, pushing global oil prices back toward $100. In the USA, the White House denied reports that defense secretary Pete Hegseth and secretary Marco Rubio are resigning following recent losses. In Ukraine, an alleged attack on a Russian humanitarian aid center killed multiple people, prompting the president to demand more air defenses. In Somalia, the Supreme Court rejected a decision extending the president's official term in office, triggering major political uncertainty across the country. In Indonesia, a massive wiretapping scandal involving senior government officials has deeply shaken political circles and triggered widespread investigations across the nation. In Kenya, a prominent doomsday co-pleter was sentenced to prison following his conviction for the murders of multiple young children. In Spain, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announced snap national elections scheduled for November 29, amid intensifying political pressure across the country. In Iraq, the foreign minister urged local armed groups to avoid involvement in any potential war between Iran and the United States. Can diplomacy prevent war in the Middle East? What do you think? In the Middle East, growing regional diplomatic efforts face massive challenges as rising military escalations continually threaten to trigger an all-out international war.
